description_full: Carnival Corporation Ltd., a cruise company, provides leisure travel services. The company operates through four segments: North America Cruise Operations, Europe Cruise Operations, Cruise Support, and Tour and Other. It operates port destinations and islands, as well as owns and operates hotels, lodges, glass-domed railcars, and motorcoaches. The company offers its services under the AIDA Cruises, Carnival Cruise Line, Costa Cruises, Cunard, Holland America Line, P&O Cruises (Australia), P&O Cruises (UK), Princess Cruises, and Seabourn brands. It sells its cruises through travel agents, tour operators, vacation planners, websites, and onboard future cruise consultants. Carnival Corporation Ltd. was founded in 1972 and is headquartered in Miami, Florida.

financial_summary: Carnival Corporation Ltd. is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $39.3B market cap on $26.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +30% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $2.6B in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.25× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.4× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 3.3×.

Shareholder yield of 2.1% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 7.2% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
